And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Niyaj Ahmad

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Nizam Ahmad
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.

Heard Mr. Niyaj Ahmad, learned counsel for the accused-applicant, Ms. Shashilata Pandey,
Advocate, holding brief of Mr. Nizam Ahmad, learned counsel for the informant/complainant, as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
Counter affidavit filed on behalf of the State as well as rejoinder affidavit filed on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. This second bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Mohd. Arif for grant of bail in Case Crime No.0191 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366 and 376 IPC read with Section 3/4 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 lodged at Police Station Jalalpur, District Ambedkar Nagar, during trial.

1 applicant has been falsely implicated in this case and, he has not committed any offence, as claimed by the prosecution.

It is further submitted that the allegation of rape and also getting pregnant by the same has been levelled in the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC, however, during the course of trial the statement of the prosecutrix and other prosecution witnesses have been recorded and the prosecutrix/victim in her statement recorded before the trial Court has stated that the statement under Section 161 CrPC, as recorded by the police, was not given by her and the statement recorded under Section 164 CrPC before the Magistrate was given by her being tutored by the police personnel.

While under cross-examination the prosecutrix/victim has stated that about two and a half years ago her brother-in-law (Jeeja) has divorced her elder sister and also that her age has been recorded in the school curtailing by 3 years.
It is also submitted that the prosecutrix in her cross examination has specifically admitted that her Nikah (marriage) had been performed with the applicant.

It is vehemently submitted that since the star witness of this crime, namely, the prosecutrix/victim has not supported the allegations, as levelled by her in her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC, chances of conviction of the applicant are remote in the trial.

It is also submitted that the statements of the prosecutrix have been recorded before the trial Court after rejection of the first bail application of the applicant and, thus, there is substantial change in circumstances since the rejection of his first bail application.
It is further submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 27.04.2023 and he is not having any previous criminal history.
Conclusion of trial would take sometime.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
4. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed a heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

5. Learned counsel for the complainant/informant submits that she under instruction is not opposing the bail plea of the applicant and she has been instructed to make a statement before this Court that informant/complainant is not having any objection if the facility of bail is extended to the applicant, moreso, when the marriage of the prosecutrix has been solemnized with the applicant and they have been blessed with a child.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is reflected that the first bail application of the applicant was dismissed by this Court as not pressed on 25.08.2023,
thus, the said order was not on merits.
After the dismissal of first bail application on 25.08.2023 statements of three prosecution witnesses have been recorded.
The victim of the crime has also been testified before the trial Court as PW-1.

Though in her chief examination she partially supported the case of the prosecution, however, in cross-examination, she has taken a U-turn and stated to have married with the applicant and also to have been blessed with a child.

She has also stated that she has not given statement, as recorded by the investigating officer under Section 161 CrPC, and the statement 164 CrPC was given by her under being tutored by the police personnel.
The applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 27.04.2023.
Certainly the recording of statements of prosecution witnesses and the statement of the prosecutrix before the trial Court is a change in circumstances.
Charge-sheet in this case has already been filed.
The applicant is not having any previous criminal antecedents and his presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial Mohd. Arif vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

7. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.
8.

Let the accused/applicant-Mohd. Arif, involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
9. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
10. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
11. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.

Order Date :- 17.1.2024 MVS/-
